Normative requirement: Identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in the product, including an SBOM in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain a component inventory and SBOM for source code, Python packages, npm packages, container images, base images, bundled services, and runtime-relevant third-party components; it should also identify and document vulnerabilities affecting those components.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is dependency-heavy and distributed as a self-hosted software stack with Python services, a React frontend, Docker images, Qdrant, MinIO, TEI, optional Open WebUI, and external provider/MCP integrations. A component inventory is needed before vulnerability monitoring or exploitability assessment can be credible.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should confirm SBOM depth, included artifacts, component criticality, and whether optional services are in assessed product scope.
Required security capability: SBOM generation; component inventory; dependency and container inventory; vulnerability intake; component-to-release traceability.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.1 SBOM Generation; §3.2 SBOM Data Quality; §3.3 Provenance & Integrity; §4.1 Vulnerability Ingestion & Monitoring
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM; dependency lockfiles; container image inventory; release artifact manifest; vulnerability register.

Normative requirement: Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay in relation to product risk, including security updates; where technically feasible, security updates should be separate from functionality updates.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should triage vulnerabilities in product context, decide remediation urgency, fix or mitigate without undue delay, and publish security releases or advisories; security-only releases should be possible where feasible for source and container distributions.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream handles credentials, corpora, provider/tool access, admin APIs, and retrieval indexes, so vulnerabilities can have confidentiality, integrity, availability, or supply-chain impact. The project needs a documented path from vulnerability discovery to fix, release, and user notification.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define severity criteria, exploitability factors, remediation SLAs, and when a security-only release is technically feasible or not.
Required security capability: Vulnerability triage; exploitability assessment; remediation planning; patch release process; security-only update decision; risk acceptance.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.2 Risk Adjudication & Vulnerability Exchange; §4.3 Actionable Decisions; §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: vulnerability records; fix PRs; release notes; advisory records; SLA matrix; risk acceptance records.

Normative requirement: Apply effective and regular tests and reviews of product security.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should perform recurring and release-gated security testing across backend APIs, frontend/admin flows, auth/RBAC, ingestion parsers, dependency/container supply chain, retrieval boundaries, MCP/tool integration, and deployment defaults.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream has multiple service boundaries and input surfaces, including API requests, admin actions, uploaded files, URLs, parser inputs, LLM/tool payloads, and configuration files. Regular security review is needed to validate both code and deployment assumptions.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should set testing frequency, depth, and techniques based on exposed interfaces, parser risk, authentication boundaries, and dependency risk.
Required security capability: SAST; dependency scanning; container scanning; DAST or API testing; parser/input security review; threat-model review; release security gate.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.4 Secure Development Properties & Security Testing; especially §3.4.5 to §3.4.10
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: CI security scans; test reports; threat model updates; API security review notes; release gate checklist.

Normative requirement: After a security update is available, share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities, including affected product identification, impacts, severity, and remediation information; delay disclosure only where justified by security risk.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should publish clear vulnerability advisories after fixes are available, identify affected versions/images/components, explain impact and severity, and provide upgrade or mitigation steps; delayed disclosure should be documented when immediate disclosure would increase risk.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: Users of a self-hosted OSS stack need actionable information to determine whether their deployed TokenStream version, container tag, optional service, or configuration is affected and how to remediate. Disclosure also supports downstream integrators using TokenStream behind their own applications.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform disclosure timing, severity classification, affected-asset identification, and when delayed publication is justified.
Required security capability: Vulnerability advisory process; affected version/component mapping; severity and impact analysis; remediation instructions; delayed-disclosure justification.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: GitHub Security Advisory; SECURITY.md process; changelog entries; advisory templates; affected-version matrix.

Normative requirement: Put in place and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should maintain and enforce a CVD policy describing how vulnerabilities are reported, acknowledged, triaged, coordinated, fixed, and disclosed, including expectations for private reporting and public issue avoidance for active vulnerabilities.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: The repository already has a SECURITY.md with private reporting guidance, but a CRA-ready process should define handling steps, ownership, timelines, reporter coordination, and disclosure criteria rather than only contact instructions.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should inform intake priorities, coordination needs for third-party components, and escalation paths for actively exploited or high-impact issues.
Required security capability: CVD policy; vulnerability intake workflow; response ownership; reporter coordination; escalation criteria; disclosure governance.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §2.1.3 CRA policy; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §4.4.7 CVD Policy
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: SECURITY.md; security contact; CVD policy; issue handling procedure; vulnerability response runbook.

Normative requirement: Facilitate sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities in the product and third-party components, including a contact address for vulnerability reporting.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should provide a clear security contact and reporting path for vulnerabilities in TokenStream code, bundled dependencies, container images, parser behavior, deployment defaults, and third-party components used by the stack.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream depends on many upstream projects and services. Users and researchers need a way to report potential vulnerabilities even when the root cause is in a dependency, container image, optional service, or integration pattern.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should clarify which third-party components are in scope, how reports are routed upstream, and how dependency-level vulnerability information is shared with users.
Required security capability: Security contact; vulnerability report intake; third-party component report handling; upstream coordination; dependency vulnerability communication.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.1 Vulnerability Ingestion & Monitoring; §4.2 Risk Adjudication & Vulnerability Exchange; §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: SECURITY.md contact address; security.txt if adopted; upstream issue links; dependency vulnerability records; reporter acknowledgement templates.

Normative requirement: Provide mechanisms to securely distribute updates so vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated in a timely manner and, where applicable for security updates, automatically.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream should distribute source releases and container images through channels that support integrity, traceability, versioning, and timely upgrade by operators; automatic update should be treated as deployment-model dependent for self-hosted OSS unless a managed updater is provided.
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream users may deploy from GitHub releases, source checkout, or container images. Secure distribution requires clear version tags, release integrity, image provenance where possible, and upgrade instructions. Automatic update is not inherently present in a self-hosted Compose stack.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should determine update channels, integrity requirements, whether automatic updates are applicable, and what mitigations exist when automatic updates are out of scope.
Required security capability: Secure update distribution; artifact integrity; release provenance; upgrade path; automatic-update applicability decision; rollback/mitigation guidance.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §3.3 Provenance & Integrity; §6.1.2 Security updates; §6.1.3 Secure software update mechanism
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: release tags; container image digests; signing or attestation records if adopted; upgrade guide; rollback notes; support/update statement.

Normative requirement: Disseminate available security updates without delay and free of charge unless otherwise agreed for tailor-made products, with advisory messages containing relevant information and user actions.
Product-specific interpretation: TokenStream security updates should be made available promptly and free of charge in the OSS distribution model, accompanied by advisory messages that explain affected versions, urgency, mitigations, upgrade steps, and any required operator actions.
Preliminary applicability: Applicable in voluntary manufacturer-like readiness scope
Preliminary applicability rationale: TokenStream is open source and non-commercial in the current scope, so charging for security updates is not expected. Users still need timely notification and practical operator guidance because deployments may contain private corpora, credentials, provider access, and connected tools.
Risk assessment dependency: Risk assessment should define notification urgency, advisory content, affected deployment scenarios, and operator action requirements for different vulnerability classes.
Required security capability: Security update publication; advisory communication; user action guidance; free-of-charge update availability; support-period communication.
OpenChain cross-check anchors: OpenChain §4.4 Disclosure & Regulatory Reporting; §6.1 Support Period & Update Obligations; §7.2 Downstream Customer Provisioning
Notes / evidence prompts: Evidence candidates: security advisory; release notes; upgrade commands; mitigation instructions; public support/update policy.
